summary: Expense Query Logic Fix Verification - ALL TESTS PASSED. Verified the fix for expense listing endpoint (GET /expenses) that was querying by employee_id (UUID) but meeting expenses stored employee_id as employee code (EMP003). Fix uses $or query to match user_id, created_by, or employee_id fields.
features_tested: GET /api/expenses - user (EMP003) can see their own meeting expenses
GET /api/expenses - user can see expenses created via POST /expenses
GET /api/expenses - admin can see all expenses
POST /api/meetings/record - creates expense with user_id, created_by, and employee_id fields
GET /api/expenses/stats/summary - user stats include meeting expenses
Admin filtering by employee_id supports both UUID and employee code

test_details.test_meeting_expense_has_correct_identit: PASS - New meeting expenses have user_id, created_by, and employee_id set correctly

test_details.test_stats_summary_includes_meeting_expe: PASS - Stats include travel category with meeting expenses
test_details.test_admin_filter_by_employee: PASS - Admin can filter by employee_id (code) or user_id (UUID)
test_details.test_verify_meeting_expenses_visible: PASS - Core fix verified - meeting expenses now visible to user

fix_verification.issue: GET /expenses returned 0 results for users because it queried by employee_id=current_user.id (UUID) but meeting expenses stored employee_id as employee code (EMP003)

fix_implementation.query_change: Changed from simple employee_id match to $or with user_id, created_by, employee_id
fix_implementation.expense_creation: Meeting expenses now include user_id (UUID), created_by (UUID), and employee_id (code)

fix_verification.status: VERIFIED - User EMP003 can now see 24 expenses including 23 meeting expenses

meetings.py_create_meeting_expense.change: Added employee_id, user_id, created_by to expense doc

seed_data_creation: Created test meetings with travel details to generate meeting expenses
context_for_next_testing_agent: Expense query fix verified. GET /expenses now uses $or query to match user_id, created_by, or employee_id. User EMP003 can see 24 expenses (23 meeting + 1 regular). Meeting expenses created via POST /meetings/record now include all identity fields (user_id, created_by, employee_id). Stats summary also updated with same $or query pattern.
